title: Evaluation of the implementation ‘Prescription for Exercise’ project in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, including medical perspectives to identify favourable and unfavourable implementation factors
summary: Exercise plays a central role in promoting our health. Scientific studies are crucial to investigate and improve the effectiveness of new interventions such as the ‘prescription for exercise’. Many people face the challenge of physical complaints, whether due to work-related stress or other everyday burdens. This often leaves little room for sporting activities or there is a lack of awareness of their importance for health. The ‘Prescription for Exercise’ programme, which has already been established in Baden-Württemberg and Hesse, addresses precisely these issues: Doctors in private practice are thus to show patients specific exercise programmes in their area with regard to their physical condition. The aim of this study is therefore to investigate the possible effects of a ‘prescription for exercise’ in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern on increasing physical activity. We also want to find out whether a doctor's recommendation for exercise can bring about a positive change in physical activity. By analysing the relationships between exercise, symptoms and prescription in more detail, we hope to gain valuable insights for the development of more effective health interventions.

Patient group: 
Patients (N=100) who receive their medical care in one of the medical practices listed above in the Greifswald model area are surveyed with an anonymous questionnaire (IPAQ) on their sitting and movement behaviour of established medical practices.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Doctors in private practice in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, especially in the city of Greifswald as a model region, who show interest in implementing the ‘Prescription for Exercise’
-	Patients who regularly receive medical care from doctors in private practice in Greifswald
-	Patients who live in a defined geographical area in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and whose medical care is in Greifswald
Exclusion criteria:
-	No consent to study participation from doctors and patients or their legal guardians
-	Insufficient language skills
